steps.tx: The World Health Organization defines **osteoporosis** by bone mineral density measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry. A **T-score of -2.5 or lower** at the lumbar spine, femoral neck, or total hip establishes osteoporosis, whereas **osteopenia** spans T-scores between **-1.0 and -2.5**. A fragility fracture of the hip or vertebra confirms osteoporosis irrespective of bone mineral density.
steps.say: The World Health Organization defines osteoporosis by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry. A T-score of -2.5 or lower or a fragility fracture establishes the diagnosis.

vis.alt: Key clinical and imaging features of osteoporosis and metabolic bone disease
vis.caption: Bone mineral density T-score categories and fragility fracture sites. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: The **FRAX tool** calculates 10-year probability of major osteoporotic and hip fractures. Clinical risk factors include age, sex, low body mass index, prior fragility fracture, parental hip fracture, current smoking, alcohol intake of **3 or more units daily**, rheumatoid arthritis, secondary osteoporosis, and systemic **glucocorticoid therapy** exceeding **5 mg daily of prednisone** for 3 months or more.
steps.say: The FRAX tool calculates ten-year probability of major osteoporotic fractures. Assessment integrates age, prior fractures, femoral neck bone density, and glucocorticoid use.

rows: Substantially increases spinal and hip risk

steps.tx: Bone remodeling reflects coupled osteoclast resorption and osteoblast formation. Osteoclast differentiation is driven by **RANKL** binding **RANK** on myeloid precursors. Osteoblasts secrete decoy receptor **osteoprotegerin** or OPG, which neutralizes RANKL. **Sclerostin**, secreted by osteocytes, inhibits **Wnt/beta-catenin signaling**, suppressing bone formation.
steps.say: Bone remodeling depends on coupled osteoclast and osteoblast activity. RANKL stimulates osteoclast resorption, while osteocyte sclerostin suppresses Wnt-mediated bone formation.

vis.alt: Bone remodeling cycle with osteoporosis drug targets shown
vis.caption: Coupled bone remodeling pathways and targeted pharmacologic intervention sites. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Oral **bisphosphonates** including **alendronate** at **70 mg weekly** and **risedronate** at **35 mg weekly** inhibit osteoclast **farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase**, inducing osteoclast apoptosis. Intravenous **zoledronic acid** at **5 mg annually** provides potent antiresorptive protection. A drug holiday is considered after **3 to 5 years** in low-risk individuals to reduce atypical femur fracture risk.
steps.say: Bisphosphonates inhibit osteoclast farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase to reduce bone resorption. Oral alendronate or annual zoledronic acid infusions provide durable fracture prevention.

nodes.label: Osteoclast apoptosis and reduced bone loss

steps.tx: **Denosumab** is a fully human monoclonal antibody that binds and neutralizes **RANKL**, administered as **60 mg subcutaneously every 6 months**. Unlike bisphosphonates, denosumab does not incorporate into bone matrix; cessation results in rapid **rebound osteoclast activation** with vertebral fractures, mandating immediate transition to a bisphosphonate if discontinued.
steps.say: Denosumab neutralizes RANKL to suppress bone resorption. Discontinuation triggers rapid rebound osteoclast activation, requiring prompt transition to a bisphosphonate.

left.title: Bisphosphonates
points: Drug holidays safe after 3 to 5 years

right.title: Denosumab
points: Circulating antibody, does not bind matrix
Rapid offset of effect at 6 months
Severe rebound vertebral fractures if stopped

steps.tx: Anabolic therapy with **teriparatide** (recombinant human **PTH 1-34** at **20 mcg daily subcutaneously**) or **abaloparatide** stimulates osteoblastic bone formation. Treatment is limited to **18 to 24 months** and is reserved for severe osteoporosis with T-scores **-3.0 or lower** or multiple vertebral fractures, followed immediately by an antiresorptive agent to preserve acquired bone.
steps.say: Teriparatide stimulates osteoblast bone formation when administered as a daily subcutaneous injection. Treatment is limited to 24 months and requires subsequent antiresorptive therapy.

nodes.label: Teriparatide 20 mcg daily for 18 to 24 months

steps.tx: **Romosozumab** is a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting **sclerostin**, exhibiting a dual action that stimulates bone formation while simultaneously decreasing bone resorption. Dosed at **210 mg subcutaneously monthly for 12 months**, it carries a boxed warning against use in patients with myocardial infarction or stroke within the preceding year.
steps.say: Romosozumab binds sclerostin to stimulate bone formation while decreasing resorption. It is administered monthly for 12 months, avoiding use in recent stroke or myocardial infarction.

rows: Produces dramatic early bone mineral density gains
Must transition to antiresorptive after 1 year
Avoid if recent MI or stroke (<1 yr)
Cardiovascular safety signal in clinical trials

steps.tx: **Osteomalacia** is defective bone matrix mineralization, predominantly caused by severe **vitamin D deficiency** with serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D below **10 to 12 ng/mL** or renal phosphate wasting. Laboratory evaluation shows low-normal calcium, low phosphate, markedly elevated **alkaline phosphatase**, and elevated parathyroid hormone. Radiographs reveal pseudofractures or **Looser zones** along compressive bone margins.
steps.say: Osteomalacia represents impaired bone mineralization from severe vitamin D deficiency or hypophosphatemia. Typical findings include elevated alkaline phosphatase and Looser zones on X-ray.

nodes.label: High alkaline phosphatase and secondary PTH rise
Impaired matrix mineralization and Looser zones
